newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-REJUVENATED FOREST BLOCK ARSENAL ADVANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REJUVENATED FOREST BLOCK ARSENAL ADVANCE.

text.p: Bottom-placed Nottingham Forest prevented Arsenal from regaining top spot in the English premier league with a thrilling 2-1 victory at the City Ground on Saturday.
Stuart Pearce's first match as player/manager looked set to end in disappointment when Ian Wright's 21st goal of the season put the London side ahead after 64 minutes.

But Norwegian Alf-Inge Haaland equalised three minutes later and Arsenal, reduced to 10 men after the combative Wright was sent off for violent conduct, were beaten when Haaland scored his second in the 89th minute.

Another Norwegian, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, hit two goals as Manchester United moved up to fourth place with a thumping 5-0 home win over Sunderland. Eric Cantona also scored twice, his first league goals for three months.
The value of overseas imports was also underlined at Chelsea where Italian Gianfranco Zola scored a fine individual goal in his new club's 3-1 success over West Ham.
